plan.name: Declare and check explored step refusals
plan.summary: Add invariant_observe.Refusal(exception_type, **attributes) and the keyword-only Step(..., refusal=None) option, matching the exact exception class and exact finite JSON scalar attribute types and values in explored runs. A declared refusal must escape the application entry on its own stack or returned awaitable before any selected call or application thread starts and leave read-back unchanged; normal returns are acceptances, all other exceptions and invalid outcomes fail, and undeclared steps and sampled runs retain their existing rules. Carry each declaration and authenticated outcome through observation validation, replay validation, attempt conversion and merging, TLC checking, fingerprints and JSON and Markdown receipts: TLC must check declared refusals against the disabled named action with its arguments and all declared acceptances against that action's actual before/after relation, including unchanged states, while receipts count declared refusals separately from legacy refusals and retain each exception. Implement the wire contract and behavior exercised and described in the acceptance files, preserve old four-field attempts and receipts for drivers without declarations, and cover the standard-library locked-slot fixture with actual Python on both supported interpreter versions and opt-in Docker execution and gate checks. Update SPEC.md and README.md with the API, strict outcome rules, receipt semantics and examples, citing existing supporting decisions including D-0200, D-0199, D-0085 and D-0122 on changed SPEC bullets; this refines D-0200 and needs a new decision recorded by whoever merges it, with decision recording and unavailable Docker or network checks reported as Merger work.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionDeclaredRefusals
tests.says: Actual Python records exact declared refusals and normal read-only acceptances, preserves their authenticated meaning through attempts and merging, and retains legacy and sampled behavior.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionDeclaredRefusalFailures
tests.says: After accepting the valid fixture, the collector rejects wrong exceptions, subclasses, mismatched attributes, target and thread exceptions, late or mutating refusals, invalid declarations and sampled refusals.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationGateDeclaredRefusals
tests.says: Explicit and legacy-selection gates carry declared outcomes to TLC and receipts; optional real Docker and TLC check the slot fixture and reject model-enabled refusals and model-disabled normal returns.

tests.name: TestDeclaredAttemptConformance
tests.says: Strict attempts retain named actions, arguments and stuttering acceptances; TLC checks refusal disabledness and acceptance relations, rejects incorrect outcomes and malformed metadata, and leaves legacy attempts unchanged.

tests.name: TestDeclaredRefusalReceipt
tests.says: JSON and Markdown receipts retain separate declared-refusal counts and exact exception attributes, explain named-action checks, and leave sampled receipt language unchanged.
